notes: Run each prompt twice: with /flow-ux and as a baseline with no skill. Grade the expectations. Serve fixtures with any static server or open them as files. The fixture has planted problems; a good review finds them by walking the flow, not by reading the source.

evals.prompt: /flow-ux Can a cafe owner sign up for Tidewell? The page is skills/flow-ux/evals/fixtures/signup.html
evals.expected_output: A walked-through review with ranked findings and a screenshot for each, starting with the blockers.
expectations: States who, task and done in three lines before the findings
Saved a screenshot for each step it walked, plus phone width
Severity 4: a failed password check wipes every field and gives no message
Severity 3 or 4: no feedback for 2.5 seconds after Next, so people click again or leave
Severity 3: labels are placeholders only, so they vanish while typing
Finds that step 2 asks for email again (redundant entry) and that the end screen gives no result or next step
Finds the tiny close button (below 24px) that reloads and loses the input
Finds that a mismatched confirm password is accepted
Every finding names its step and screenshot path; no finding is based on the source code alone
Reports the check-page.mjs summary line for the page
Changes no files in review mode; the reply is 5 lines or fewer and leads with the verdict and severity counts

evals.prompt: /flow-ux fix the sign-up flow in skills/flow-ux/evals/fixtures/signup.html (work on a copy)
evals.expected_output: A fixed copy where no severity 4 or 3 problem remains, proven by walking it again.
expectations: Works on a copy, not the fixture
Fixes in severity order and shows before and after screenshots for each fixed finding
Input survives a failed submit and the error says what to change, next to the field
Visible labels above every field; the primary buttons say what they do
The duplicate email field is gone and the end screen says what happened and what to do next
Walks the whole flow again (happy, mistake, keyboard, phone) after fixing
check-page.mjs exits 0 on the fixed copy

evals.prompt: /design Build a two-step checkout form (HTML) for a plant shop: delivery details, then payment summary.
evals.expected_output: Design pulls in the flow-ux rules and the form is right first time.
expectations: The reply says it applied flow-ux's rules
Shows 'Step 1 of 2' with step names
Labels above fields, autocomplete and input types set on name, address, email and phone
The primary button names its action (for example 'Continue to payment')
check-page.mjs exits 0
